newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian stocks fall on news of Yeltsin heart operation.
newsitem.headline: Russian stocks fall on news of Yeltsin heart operation.

text.p: Stock prices fell sharply Thursday on news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had agreed to a heart operation but the market managed to cut its loss.

"The thing's gone down, everybody is selling, and it's not looking good," said Nick Mokhoff, head of equities trading at Alliance-Menatep. He reckoned that stocks were likely to fall further on Friday.
The Russian Trading System Index of 21 leading stocks fell 1.17 percent in active trading.
On the New York Stock Exchange, the Templeton Russia Fund, the only closed-end fund that trades exclusively in Russian companies, fell 75 cents to $20.875.

Yeltsin, breaking a taboo observed by generations of Kremlin leaders, admitted to Russians Thursday in a television interview that he was in poor health and had agreed to heart surgery at the end of the month.

A Kremlin source told Reuters the operation was likely to be bypass surgery, in which artificial tubes are inserted to replace clogged arteries to improve blood supply to the heart. Bypass patients can return to active working lives within a month or so of surgery and can go on to live for many years.

Yeltsin's announcement came at the start of a new four-year term, as Russia grapples with economic problems and the aftermath of war in Chechnya. In a land where poor health has traditionally meant waning political power it was a bold step.
Many traders said the market could fall until an announcement of the outcome of Yeltsin's operation, or news that the operation was not serious.
